paragraphs.text: Congenital hypomyelinating neuropathy is a hereditary demyelinating peripheral neuropathy that begins in early infancy. Its features include distal muscle weakness, hypotonia, areflexia, and severely slowed nerve conduction velocities (Mandich et al., 1999). Onset may be prenatal, neonatal, or early infantile. Histopathologically, myelin sheaths are absent or thin, and most of the few patients described in the literature die within the first years of life (Smit et al., 2008).

paragraphs.text: Mandich et al. (1999) described the clinical, morphologic, and immunohistochemical features of a patient with congenital hypomyelination. The patient's clinical features were quite distinct from those of the more frequent forms of MPZ-related neuropathy, Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 1B (CMT1B) and Dejerine-Sottas syndrome (DSS).

paragraphs.text: Kochanski et al. (2004) and Smit et al. (2008) noted that congenital hypomyelinating neuropathy has been associated with mutations in several genes: MPZ, EGR2, PMP22, and MTMR2. Kochanski et al. (2004) stated that the disorder can be inherited as either an autosomal dominant or an autosomal recessive trait.

paragraphs.text: Warner et al. (1996) identified 5 novel mutations in the MPZ gene, which encodes P0, the major structural protein of peripheral nerve myelin. These mutations were found in patients with CMT1B, DSS, or congenital hypomyelination. The authors suggested that these disorders may not be distinct pathophysiologic entities but rather a spectrum of related 'myelinopathies' caused by an underlying defect in myelination.

paragraphs.text: In a patient with congenital hypomyelination, Mandich et al. (1999) identified a de novo gln215-to-ter (Q215X) mutation in the MPZ gene. They concluded that this finding confirmed that congenital hypomyelination is allelic with disorders that have a less severe phenotype and a different clinical and neuropathologic profile.

paragraphs.text: In a patient with congenital hypomyelination, Szigeti et al. (2003) identified a complex de novo mutation in the MPZ gene.
